title: Intro: What is Loop Engineering?
text: Hey, I'm Muskin. When I first heard about loop engineering, my honest first thought was, wouldn't this cost me way more tokens and more money? Fair question. But it turns out that isn't the question that decides whether a loop is worth building. Let's open it up. So, what is a loop? Instead of prompting the AI turn by turn, you build a system that prompts it for you. It triggers itself, runs, checks its own work, and decides the next step with no human in each run. Boris Cherny, who leads Cloud Code, says

title: The Cost Question: Tokens vs. Time
text: His job now is writing loops. Here's the refrain. Yes, loops cost more per task than a single prompt, repeated context, extra tool calls, iteration. But that's the wrong place to stop. The real question isn't what a loop costs, it's whether it saves you enough time to be worth it. Before you build one, two things have to be true. title: The Two Requirements: Clear triggers and stop conditions
text: File change. Second, a verifiable exit condition, tests passing, a metric clearing, or a human approving. Miss the trigger and it never runs. Miss the exit and it never stops. Let's run a real task through it, nightly dependency updates. Is there a clear trigger? A nightly schedule, yes. A verifiable exit? The test suite passes, yes. Can it check itself? title: Case Study: Earning a loop with nightly dependency updates
text: This one earns a loop. That's the sweet spot, repetitive repetitive, well-defined, high-volume work. Nightly refactors, babysitting pull request reviews and tests, reconciling invoices or data, overnight code you review with your morning coffee. Clear task, repeats often, easy to check. title: Where Loops Blow Up: One-off, judgment-heavy work
text: Check success. And high-frequency runs with no caps, agents stuck retrying forever, burning real money. Looking busy is not the same as being done. If you do build one, keep the cost sane. Cap iterations, time, and spend. Use cheap models to generate, strong ones to verify. Externalize the context you repeat into skills or caching, and

title: Keeping Costs Sane: Iteration caps and deterministic checks
text: Prefer deterministic checks, tests, and linters over the AI grading itself. So, here's the whole thing on one page. Loop engineering isn't a free upgrade, it's infrastructure. Before you build, ask, is there a trigger and a stop condition? Can verification run on its own? Does it repeat enough to earn the setup? If yes, build it. If no, a plain prompt still wins.
